title: Slices, Maps & Arrays
intro: Slices and maps are the workhorse data structures in Go, and the interview questions around them test whether you understand what's happening under the hood. This module covers the array vs slice distinction (arrays have fixed length at compile time and are value types; slices are descriptors pointing to an underlying array), the three-field slice header (pointer, len, cap), append and what happens when capacity is exceeded (a new, larger array is allocated and the slice descriptor is updated — why this means append can return a different backing array), the common slice tricks (copy, delete element by index, two-pointer for filter-in-place), maps with make and map literals, map zero values (reading a missing key returns the zero value; writing to a nil map panics — the check-existence idiom: v, ok := m[k]), safe concurrent map access (sync.Map or map + Mutex), and ranging over slices and maps. Every answer includes the gotcha the interviewer is testing.
